title: 材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Strength of Materials I
keywords: Stress, Strain 2.Tension, Compression 3.Bending moment of beam 4.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Investigating the strength of materials can clarify the forces that act on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, living tissues and cells, etc., and the deformations they cause. The results can be used for safety design. It is therefore a foundational subject in mechanical engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the investigation of the strength of materials through lectures and practice.
advice: This is a basic strength of materials course. We will cover the following topics: 1. Stress and strain 6. Statically indeterminate problems 2. Hooke’s law 7. Thermal stress and stress concentration 3. Mechanical properties of materials 8. Thin-walled cylinders subjected to internal pressure 4. Allowable stress and safety factors 9. Beams and their support conditions 5. Frame structure 10. Shearing forces and bending moments of beams In this course, it is important to do many practice exercises, but the study of the strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand just by memorizing formulas and patterns. To solve a problem, one should start with an understanding of the basic formulas needed, and then set the appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. In addition, it is necessary to be able to concretely imagine the actual forces, moments, and deformations using schematic diagrams. Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
books: Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reference books: Basic Strength of Materials, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese) Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Gaining understanding by working through many different problems is the best way to learn strength of materials. As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand "Industrial Mechanics I". In addition, students will be expected to move on to "Strength of Materials II" and "Strength of Materials III", which will be offered subsequently, as they are applications of this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain, and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain the deformation and fracture behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain the relationship between material properties, reference strength, and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain the frame structure, thermal stress, thin-walled cylinders and stress concentration.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment generated in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1. Understand the concept of stress and strain. 2. Distinguish the nominal stress and true stress, nominal strain and true strain. 3. Design safe structures using standard strength and allowable stress. 4. Design safe structures in frame structures, thermal stress problems, a thin-walled cylinder subject to internal pressure. 5 Draw SFDs and BMDs for various beams loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load. 6. Understand in depth the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. Calculate stresses and strains. 2. Perform calculations on the basis of safety factors. 3. Calculate stresses in a frame structure and a thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure, and in a thermal stress problem. 4. Draw SFDs and BMDs of a cantilever beam and a simple support beam loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load. 5. Understand the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

lessons.content: Course introduction Review the mathematics and mechanics necessary to understand Strength of Materials I. Understand the policies of this course and learn the basics of strength of materials. Learn to convert between SI units and engineering units.
lessons.assignments: Review in advance the trigonometric functions, force resolution, synthesis, translation, force balance, and moments. Read pp. 1 to 4 in the text carefully. Review class content and solve related exercises.
Read pp. 4-6 and 7-9 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Learn about strain and Hooke's law.
lessons.assignments: Read pp. 7-9 and 9-11 of the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Learn about the mechanical properties of materials, allowable stress, and safety factors.
lessons.assignments: Read pp. 11-14 and 14-15 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Answer exercises related to classes 1 to 4 and discuss them in a group and deepen their understanding.
lessons.assignments: Submit a report. As a review, solve exercises on the material in Chapter 1.

lessons.content: First test is given. Review materials from classes 1 to 5. Learn about frame structures.

lessons.assignments: Read pp. 33-35 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Learn about stress concentration and a thin- walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure.
lessons.assignments: Read pp. 36-39 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Answer exercises related to classes 6 to 8 and discuss in a group, and deepen their understanding.
Second test is given. Review material from classes 6 to 9. Learn about beams and support conditions for beams.
lessons.operation: Test and review Lecture Practice Q&A Self-check
lessons.assignments: Solve exercises related to classes 6 to 9. Review points that you did not understand in the test. Read pp. 45-48 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note.

lessons.content: Learn about shearing force and bending moment in beams.
lessons.assignments: Read pp. 48-52 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Learn about shearing force and bending moment in beams and the relationship between shearing force and bending moment.
lessons.assignments: Read pp. 53-58 in the text and summarize them in a preparatory note. Review class content and solve related exercises.

lessons.content: Answer exercises on material in classes 10 to 12 and discuss in a group, and deepen their understanding.
lessons.assignments: Submit a report. Review class content and solve related exercises. As a review, solve the exercises related to Chapter 3.
Solve exercises related to classes 1 to 13 to deepen understanding.
